# What is Canvas?

#### Course: Canvas Foundations

## What is Canvas?

So far, we have talked about the game you will build and the tools you will use.

Now it is time to start working with canvas.

A canvas is a rectangular drawing surface built right into the browser. Canvas gives us a space where JavaScript can draw shapes directly on the screen. Those shapes will eventually become the paddle, the bricks, and the ball in our Brick Breaker game.

Nothing happens until you connect it to JavaScript. That connection happens in two lines.

```html
1<!DOCTYPE html>
2<html lang="en">
3    <head>
4        <meta charset="UTF-8">
5        <title>Canvas</title>
6        <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">
7    </head>
8    <body>
9        <canvas id="gameCanvas" width="400" height="300">
10        </canvas>
11        <script src="script.js">
12        </script>
13    </body>
14</html>
```

```css
1*  {
2    margin: 0;
3    padding: 0;
4    box-sizing: border-box;
5}
6body  {
7    display: flex;
8    justify-content: center;
9    align-items: center;
10    height: 100vh;
11    background: #f0f0f0;
12}
13canvas  {
14    display: block;
15    border: 1px solid #ccc;
16    background: #fff;
17}
```

```javascript
1const canvas = document.getElementById("gameCanvas");
2const ctx = canvas.getContext("2d");
3ctx.fillRect(50, 50, 100, 60);
```

Click Run Code and you will see a small black rectangle appear on the canvas.

Here is what each line does:

- getElementById("gameCanvas"): grabs the canvas element from the HTML
- getContext("2d"): hands you back a drawing toolkit packed with every method you need to draw shapes, text, and images
- fillRect(50, 50, 100, 60): draws a filled rectangle at position x=50, y=50 with width=100 and height=60

![Canvas HTML element connected by arrow to the 2D context object](data:application/octet-stream;base64,)

One small habit worth building now. Always name it ctx. Every canvas developer uses that name. If someone else reads your code, they will know exactly what it is without thinking twice.

Next, you will learn how the canvas coordinate system works, because knowing where (0, 0) lives changes everything.
